sections.text: Introduction

The thermal and air hazards of Damietta power station resulted from or 
 referred to the harmful effect of exposure of workers in their ( sites of 
 work) to high degree of emitted flue gases more than the permissible value 
 according to the law of
 environment (4) year 1994. 
 Therefore the environmental administration in Damietta power station make
 a scientific program in order to avoid and protect all the worked persons in 
 the station from the hazards.

Madur GA-40 plus is the microprocessor controlled gas analyser, it is a high 
 quality instrument produced using the latest technical discoveries.

The first draft initiated by chem. Yasser 
 Lotfy Zahra tested by chem. Mohamed Elsaied Eshra, reviewed by general 
 manager chemist Anis Abou Elez, revised by quality control chemist Wael A. 
 Tantawy at EDEPCo. And accepted by eng.Monier EL Wakel ,head sector of 
 Damietta P.S.
Information
The GA-40 plus is a multi functional flue gas analyser.
Electrochemical Sensors are used for the measurement of gas concentration.
The instrument can be fitted between 2 and 6 of these sensors.

All analysers are fitted with O2 and CO sensors, further gas cells 
 must be chosen when the instrument is ordered. The GA-40 analyser containing 3 
 cells, the third one being an NO sensor.
Oxygen, O2
Carbon monoxide Co
Nitric oxide No
Carbon dioxide CO2
Nitrogen oxide NOx

The first three gases (O2,CO,No) are measured directly using the 
 electrochemical cells.The remaining components are calculated.

The concentration of oxygen and carbon dioxide are shown in percent. The 
 concentration of the remaining gases is shown as follows:
Volume concentration in [ppm],

Absolute 
mass concentration in [mg/m3],

Mass 
concentration relative to the oxygen content in [mg/m3],
Mass concentration relative to the energy output in [mg/MJ].

In addition the air inlet or ambient temperature at a broad range of ambient 
 temperature (0-50oC ) and the flue gas temperature are measured. 
 It is fitted with a rechargeable battery making it independent of the mains 
 power supply.
Construction
Fig (1) shows a block diagram of the GA-40 plus.

Here 
 is a description of the individual components.
Element of Gas Circuit

Gas 
Probe with inLine Filter- 
 The gas probe is used to extract the gases under investigation and to measure 
 their temperature. The gas probe consists of two parts, the probe pipe with 
 thermocouple (1) and the probe holder (2). As 
 standard a Ni-CrNi thermocouple is used.

Gas Pump- 
 The internal gas pump draws the gas into the GA-40 plus and passes it through 
the gas chambers. The gas cells operate best with a flow rate of 90 l/h.

Gas Chamber- 
 The gas chamber is fitted with between two and six sensors and is 
characterized by minimal dead capacity.
Measurement System

Gas 
Sensors- 
 The oxygen concentration and the toxic gases are measured using an 
electrochemical cells.
Table present all the gas sensors available.

Ambient Air Temperature Sensor-
 The ambient air temperature is measured by the analyzer for 
 use in some of calculations carried out.

Flue Gas Temperature Sensor- 
 The range of such a thermocouple is 40 800oC in the standard version 
 (1100oC available optionally).

Differential 
Pressure 
Sensor- 
 The measuring range of the pressure sensor is +/- 50 hPa.
Power Supply

The maintenance free 12V battery used has a capacity of 2.6 Ah. A fully 
 charged battery will power the instrument for about five hours.

Calculating the Concentration of Nitrogen Oxide NOX

In addition to nitric oxide NO, combustion gases 
contain also higher oxides of nitrogen (mainly NO2), it is possible 
to calculate the NO2 contents on the basis of the measured NO. 
It is generally assumed that nitric oxide NO contained in combustion gases makes 
up about 95% of the total amount of nitrogen oxides NOX.
NO (ppm)

If the optional sensor of the GA-40 plus analyser 
is the NO2 sensor there is no need to calculate the amount of NO2.Then 
the NOX concentration is calculated by the analyser as a simple sum of measured 
NO and NO2 concentrations.

NOX (ppm) = NO (ppm) + 
NO2 (ppm)

Directives

Gas Sensors- 
The following points are important for maximising 
the operational life of the cells and achieving measurements without errors.
Don't exceed the rated concentration;

All the gas cells may react unpredictably to the 
presence of substances which aren't usually found in flue gases. For this 
reason, the analyser may not be cleaned with chemical solvents. If organic 
solvents enter the gas chamber, the cells may become unstable or even suffer 
permanent damage;

Some cells require the presence of a bias voltage 
when not in use. don't allow the battery to become fully discharged;

Don't switch the analyser off before the system is 
purged of remaining flue gas;

Store the analyser in a cool place to reduce the 
ageing of the cells.

sections.text:
Gas System- 
The gas system of the analyser is protected by a 
double in-line filter.

Battery- 
When the voltage drops below 11 V. an acoustic 
warning signal is given, the GA-40 plus will switch off automatically if the 
voltage drops below 10.5 V. The analyser will operate for about 5 hours from the 
battery. N.B. Some parts of the analyser draw current even when 
the device is switched off. If the analyser isn't being used then the battery 
should be charged fully at least once a month.

Service Intervals-
The parameters of the electrochemical 
cells change with time, and therefore service periodically is necessary by 
re-calibration of the gas sensors using test gases. The recommended service 
interval is 800 operating hours or 6 months. The operating time and the number 
of hours until the next service are shown in SERVICE/DEVICE INFO.

Errors during Operation-
The analyser checks all circuitry 
continuously. When the message " ERROR" appear on the screen, the error can be 
found shown on the screen OPTIONS/SERVICE/CONTROL LIST.

Switching off after Use-
The operating life of the 
electrochemical cells is dependent on the usage of the instrument. The wear and 
tear on the cells is greater when the cell is exposed to the gas for longer or 
the concentration is higher. The gas cell is hence "used up" during 
measurements. For this reason, the analyser shouldn't be switched off until 
all the gas tubing has been completely cleared of flue gases and the gas cells 
have been purged with fresh air for several minutes.
